Subject: [PATCH] ext4: avoid allocate block from corrupted group in
 ext4_mb_find_by_goal()

There's issue as follows:
...

EXT4-fs (mmcblk0p1): Delayed block allocation failed for inode 2239 at logical offset 0 with max blocks 1 with error 117
EXT4-fs (mmcblk0p1): This should not happen!! Data will be lost

EXT4-fs (mmcblk0p1): error count since last fsck: 1
EXT4-fs (mmcblk0p1): initial error at time 1765597433: ext4_mb_generate_buddy:760
EXT4-fs (mmcblk0p1): last error at time 1765597433: ext4_mb_generate_buddy:760
...

According to the log analysis, blocks are always requested from the
corrupted block group. This may happen as follows:
ext4_mb_find_by_goal
  ext4_mb_load_buddy
   ext4_mb_load_buddy_gfp
     ext4_mb_init_cache
      ext4_read_block_bitmap_nowait
      ext4_wait_block_bitmap
       ext4_validate_block_bitmap
        if (!grp || EXT4_MB_GRP_BBITMAP_CORRUPT(grp))
         return -EFSCORRUPTED; // There's no logs.
 if (err)
  return err;  // Will return error
ext4_lock_group(ac->ac_sb, group);
  if (unlikely(EXT4_MB_GRP_BBITMAP_CORRUPT(e4b->bd_info))) // Unreachable
   goto out;

After commit 9008a58e5dce ("ext4: make the bitmap read routines return
real error codes") merged, Commit 163a203ddb36 ("ext4: mark block group
as corrupt on block bitmap error") is no real solution for allocating
blocks from corrupted block groups. This is because if
'EXT4_MB_GRP_BBITMAP_CORRUPT(e4b->bd_info)' is true, then
'ext4_mb_load_buddy()' may return an error. This means that the block
allocation will fail.
Therefore, check block group if corrupted when ext4_mb_load_buddy()
returns error.

Fixes: 163a203ddb36 ("ext4: mark block group as corrupt on block bitmap error")
Fixes: 9008a58e5dce ("ext4: make the bitmap read routines return real error codes")
Signed-off-by: Ye Bin <yebin10@huawei.com>
Reviewed-by: Ritesh Harjani (IBM) <ritesh.list@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Zhang Yi <yi.zhang@huawei.com>
Reviewed-by: Andreas Dilger <adilger@dilger.ca>
Reviewed-by: Jan Kara <jack@suse.cz>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260302134619.3145520-1-yebin@huaweicloud.com
Signed-off-by: Theodore Ts'o <tytso@mit.edu>
Cc: stable@kernel.org

diff --git a/fs/ext4/mballoc.c b/fs/ext4/mballoc.c
index 20e9fdaf4301..705a879f13d3 100644
--- a/fs/ext4/mballoc.c
+++ b/fs/ext4/mballoc.c
@@ -2443,8 +2443,12 @@ int ext4_mb_find_by_goal(struct ext4_allocation_context *ac,
 		return 0;
 
 	err = ext4_mb_load_buddy(ac->ac_sb, group, e4b);
-	if (err)
+	if (err) {
+		if (EXT4_MB_GRP_BBITMAP_CORRUPT(e4b->bd_info) &&
+		    !(ac->ac_flags & EXT4_MB_HINT_GOAL_ONLY))
+			return 0;
 		return err;
+	}
 
 	ext4_lock_group(ac->ac_sb, group);
 	if (unlikely(EXT4_MB_GRP_BBITMAP_CORRUPT(e4b->bd_info)))
-- 
2.34.1

The patch modifies a single file `fs/ext4/mballoc.c` to prevent allocation failures caused by corrupted block groups.

**Modification in `fs/ext4/mballoc.c`**:
- In function `ext4_mb_find_by_goal()`, after `ext4_mb_load_buddy()` returns an error (`err`), a new condition is added:
  - If the error is due to a corrupted block bitmap (`EXT4_MB_GRP_BBITMAP_CORRUPT`) **and** the allocation does not have the `EXT4_MB_HINT_GOAL_ONLY` flag, the function returns `0` (success) instead of the error.
  - Otherwise, the error is returned as before.

This change ensures that when a block group is marked as corrupted, the allocation request does not fail immediately but instead allows the allocator to skip the corrupted group and continue searching other groups.

**Relationship**:
The fix addresses a regression introduced by two prior commits: `9008a58e5dce` ("ext4: make the bitmap read routines return real error codes") and `163a203ddb36` ("ext4: mark block group as corrupt on block bitmap error"). After these commits, `ext4_mb_load_buddy()` would return an error for corrupted groups, but the caller `ext4_mb_find_by_goal()` did not handle this error by skipping the group; it simply propagated the error, leading to repeated allocation failures. The patch adds the missing check to treat the error from a corrupted group as a non-fatal situation, allowing the allocation to retry with other groups.

Root cause:
After commits 9008a58e5dce and 163a203ddb36, `ext4_mb_load_buddy()` returns an error when the block group bitmap is corrupted. In `ext4_mb_find_by_goal()`, this error is returned immediately without checking if the corruption was the cause. As a result, the allocator fails and repeats the same request on the same corrupted group, causing allocation failure and data loss. The intended behavior is to skip the corrupted group and continue searching.

Code statements information:
The code statements that lead to the bug are:
<text>
if (err)
    return err;
</text>
Reason:
This unconditionally returns the error from `ext4_mb_load_buddy()` when the block group bitmap is corrupted. Since `ext4_mb_load_buddy()` marks the group as corrupt and returns an error, the allocation fails. The allocator may then retry the same group, leading to repeated allocation failures and data loss. The intended behavior is to skip the corrupted group when the allocation does not require that exact group.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
<text>
if (err) {
    if (EXT4_MB_GRP_BBITMAP_CORRUPT(e4b->bd_info) &&
        !(ac->ac_flags & EXT4_MB_HINT_GOAL_ONLY))
        return 0;
    return err;
}
</text>
Reason:
This checks if the error was due to a corrupted block group bitmap. If the group is corrupted and the allocation is not strictly goal-only (i.e., the allocator can try other groups), it returns 0 to indicate that no block was found from this group. This allows the allocator to continue searching other groups instead of failing outright. If the allocation must use the exact group (GOAL_ONLY), the error is still returned to avoid silent failures.
